outlook.statement: On account of overall economic slowdown, liquidity crisis faced by the Company and investments being blocked, your Company is striving hard to capture its business opportunities and also trying for new avenues to provide impetus to the operations of the Company and achieve target as per business plan of the Company.

The NBFC sector is positioned for sustained double-digit growth in the medium term, supported by digital adoption, government policy support, and underserved market penetration. The sector's systemic significance means it will remain under close regulatory watch, but reforms (co-lending, capital norms) are expected to make it more resilient and competitive.

The sector is projected to maintain 15–17% credit growth CAGR between FY24 and FY27, driven by MSME lending, retail finance, and co-lending models. NBFCs' role in bridging the credit gap will keep them central to India's financial ecosystem. Strong demand, technological advancement, and policy support point to sustained growth, although profitability will hinge on effective cost control, prudent risk management, and diversification.

The NBFC sector is projected to maintain a steady 16–18% credit growth rate, with overall Assets Under Management (AUM) securely on track to cross the ₹50 lakh crore threshold by March 2027. Growth is primarily anchored by secured MSME lending, vehicle finance, and a high-performing gold loan segment. The NBFC-MFI segment faced a steep deceleration down to 4% growth in FY26 due to localized asset quality stress, though a cyclical rebound to 20% is projected for FY27. Average sector Return on Assets (RoA) remains healthy at 2.2% to 2.4%. Peak Net Interest Margins (NIMs) are facing minor compression due to rising bank-linked borrowing costs.

risks: overall economic slowdown
liquidity crisis faced by the Company
investments being blocked
AI-enabled cyber threats ranked as the single most critical risk over the next 12 months by RBI survey of banks and Upper-Layer NBFCs
Stricter risk-weight mandates from RBI causing deliberate cooling of unsecured retail segments
Rising localized credit stress and aggressive portfolio write-offs in NBFC-MFI sector
Industry-wide rise in bank-linked borrowing costs compressing Net Interest Margins (NIMs)
Regulatory-driven calibration causing intentional deceleration in unsecured assets
Non-compliance with SEBI regulation requiring 100% promoter holding in demat form
Delay in filing mandatory returns with RBI due to technical problems
Unlike banks, NBFCs cannot accept low-cost demand deposits and depend on bank borrowings or market instruments.
Rapid changes in monetary policy can compress spreads and increase funding costs.
Intensifying competition from fintechs, payment banks, and aggressive bank lending in retail and SME segments.
Convergence of NBFC norms with bank regulations on capital adequacy, provisioning, and disclosure may pressure smaller NBFCs.
Overexposure to high-risk borrower categories could raise NPAs if macro conditions deteriorate.
Economic slowdown, currency volatility, and geopolitical events could dampen credit demand.
Smaller NBFCs still face difficulties in maintaining adequate liquidity buffers.
Scale-Based Regulation framework requires stronger governance, risk management, and capital, increasing operational costs.
Maintaining low NPAs in the face of rapid loan growth requires stronger underwriting and recovery mechanisms.
Low switching costs require continuous innovation in service delivery to retain clients.
Digital adoption brings cyber security risks and the need for substantial IT investment.
AI-driven cyber vulnerabilities and high third-party vendor concentrations flagged by RBI.
